recipes.name: Dodo (Nigerian Fried Ripe Plantain)
recipes.description: Ripe plantain slices with soft centres and browned edges, served warm beside rice or beans.
recipes.story: Yellow plantains with dark speckles soften and sweeten as they ripen. Dodo is a familiar side for Nigerian rice and bean dishes.

ingredients.name: neutral frying oil
ingredients.prep_note: pan supply, not a serving amount; adjust to the pan and reuse across batches

steps.title: Peel and slice
steps.instruction: Trim each plantain at both ends. Slit the skin lengthwise and lift it away. Cut the flesh diagonally into slices about 1 cm thick.

steps.title: Prepare the pan
steps.instruction: Season the slices lightly with the salt if using. Put enough oil in a small, deep frying pan to cover its base generously. Warm over medium heat until the edge of a test slice sizzles.

steps.title: Fry in batches
steps.instruction: Lower a single layer of slices into the oil with tongs. Check the undersides after about three minutes. Turn when golden and cook the second face until browned and tender. Reduce the heat if the colour develops too quickly.

steps.title: Drain and serve
steps.instruction: Lift the slices onto a rack or absorbent paper. Cook the remaining slices in the same oil and serve the dodo warm.
